title: Correlated impulses: Using Facebook interests to improve predictions of crime rates in urban areas
geography: United States (Baltimore, Boston, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles, New York, Philadelphia, San Francisco, Washington)
thesis: Facebook interests can improve predictions of crime rates in urban areas beyond demographic factors.
theme_1_justification: Not addressed. No discussion of dual-use, technology transfer, or properties of software/data.
theme_2_justification: Tangential mention of algorithmic opacity: 'The Facebook algorithms that generate the data are a black box' (Discussion). No deep engagement with epistemic authority or surveillance.
theme_3_justification: Not addressed. The paper does not conceptualize the city as a programmable system or discuss modulation.
theme_4_justification: Not addressed. No discussion of spatial destruction, home unmaking, or urban warfare.
key_quotes: The Facebook algorithms that generate the data are a black box, creating two issues. The first is one of substantive interpretation and what exactly it means for a particular ZIP code to be high in a given interest. The second is that changes in these algorithms would mean that the models need to be re-calibrated over time for long-term prediction purposes.
Last, there is a general caveat for modern digital data resources: 'researcher beware' [40–42].
This study is exploratory, thus we propose no a priori hypotheses linking particular preferences to a given theory of criminality.
